Astronics (ATRO) appeared in search results as an aerospace/defense electronics and test-systems supplier with Boeing customer concentration; it was not included due to the four-candidate limit but should be revisited as a possible testing/certification-gate candidate.

The strongest node signal is not generic defense revenue; it is evidence of qualification barriers, long-cycle defense backlog, specialized manufacturing processes, customer concentration with primes or Navy programs, and limited alternate-source capacity.

node: Defense subtier components and qualified industrial suppliers
summary: Expanded the universe for the defense subtier-components node with a two-lane funnel. HEICO is included only as a reference/context anchor because it illustrates the already-recognized niche aerospace/defense components model at large scale. The underfollowed lane prioritizes smaller US-listed suppliers where defense exposure is embedded inside aerospace, engineered-products, composite-materials, or industrial manufacturing labels. Key chokepoint signals to verify in later layers are prime-contractor qualification, DoD/Navy program concentration, long-cycle backlog, certified or specialized manufacturing processes, and customer concentration that may reveal hidden prime/subprime dependency.
